The DCT Transform Method is a value compression technique for TSDF volumes that partitions data into blocks and subblocks, transforms them using the 3D Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), and entropy codes the resulting coefficients [S1][S2].

The claim states that the DCT Transform Method partitions data into blocks and subblocks, transforms them using 3D DCT, and entropy codes the coefficients. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'DCT transform method [YL95] partitions data in blocks, which are further subdivided into subblocks. Subsequently subblocks are transformed by the DCT... DC coefficients are grouped quantized and delta encoded, while AC coefficients are compressed as previously described for the DFT approach [which uses run-length and Huffman encoding].' Source [S2] confirms this exact process. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

It partitions data into blocks and subblocks, transforms them using the 3D DCT, and entropy codes the coefficients using a pipeline analogous to 2D JPEG lossy compression [S1][S2].

The claim states that the method partitions data into blocks and subblocks, transforms them using 3D DCT, and entropy codes coefficients using a pipeline analogous to 2D JPEG lossy compression. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'DCT transform method [YL95] partitions data in blocks, which are further subdivided into subblocks. Subsequently subblocks are transformed by the DCT, as what is done in 2D with JPEG lossy compression.' It further details that DC coefficients are grouped, quantized, and delta encoded, while AC coefficients are compressed using zigzag ordering, run-length, and Huffman encoding (the standard JPEG pipeline). Source [S2] corroborates these exact details. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
